name: regulus
label: Regulus (alpha Leo A, B8 IVn, rapid rotator)

sources: McAlister et al. 2005: equatorial 1.65 / polar 1.25 mas, polar axis at PA 85.5 deg
notes: Major axis (the equator) at PA 175.5 deg E of N.

sources: McAlister et al. 2005, ApJ 628, 439 (CHARA, Roche model): polar diameter 1.25 +/- 0.02 mas, equatorial 1.65 +/- 0.02 mas (axis ratio 1.32), polar-axis PA 85.5 +/- 2.8 deg, i 90 (+0/-15) deg, V sin i 317 km/s (V/V_crit 0.86), T_pol 15400, T_eq 10314 K, mass 3.4 Msun, gravity-darkening beta 0.25
Gies et al. 2008 / modern: mass 4.15 Msun; van Leeuwen 2007: parallax 41.13 +/- 0.35 mas (24.3 pc); V 1.40; H, K ~1.6 (approximate)
notes: theta_ld_mas 1.436 = sqrt(1.65 x 1.25), the equal-area diameter; the `ellipse` block carries the shape (major axis along PA 175.5 deg = polar axis 85.5 + 90; the axis is ambiguous by 180 deg).

Regulus Ab (a 0.3 Msun white dwarf in a 40.1 d orbit) contributes negligible light; B and C at 177 arcsec are excluded by any field stop. i ~ 90 so the projected shape is the true flattening. Gravity darkening not modelled.
First null of the equal-area disk at 650 nm: 114 m; the oblateness campaigns use the ISI triangle with 70 m sides.
Anchors are Vega magnitudes converted with the band table's Vega -> AB offsets (V +0.02, H +1.39, K +1.85).
The radius is derived from theta_LD and the distance.
assumptions: ellipse (uniform-brightness affine disk; no gravity darkening)
